title.rendered: Let Not Your Hearts Be Troubled: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “Let not your hearts be troubled. Believe in God; believe also in me.” A morning devotional on the command that is also a comfort.

content.rendered:
The upper room in Jerusalem, on the night before the cross. Jesus knew what was coming in the next twenty-four hours. His disciples did not. Their world was about to unravel. His first words to them that night were words of steadying comfort.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, September 15, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Let not your heart be troubled; you believe in God, believe also in Me. In My Father’s house are many mansions; if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.”
John 14:1-2 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

The upper room in Jerusalem, on the night before the cross. A rented room somewhere in the old city, the low table set for the Passover meal, twelve men and one Rabbi in the flickering lamplight. Jesus knew what was coming in the next twenty-four hours. Judas would leave the table and slip into the night to betray Him. He would pray in agony in Gethsemane. He would be arrested, tried, beaten, mocked, crucified. He would breathe His last on a Roman cross by three in the afternoon on Friday. His disciples did not know most of this yet. But they could feel that something was wrong. Their teacher was speaking about leaving. He had just told them one of them would betray Him. The room was heavy with uncertainty. And into that room, Jesus spoke words that have steadied believers for two thousand years. “Let not your heart be troubled.”

He did not deny that trouble was coming. He did not pretend the disciples were wrong to feel what they were feeling. He simply set their gaze on something bigger than the trouble. “You believe in God, believe also in Me. In My Father’s house are many mansions; if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.” Whatever was about to happen on Friday, the destination on the other side of it was the Father’s house. Whatever loss the disciples were about to experience, Jesus Himself was preparing their place. The trouble in the room was real. But the trouble in the room was not the last word. The Father’s house was.

The Passion Translation renders it with striking depth: “Don’t worry or surrender to your fear. For you’ve believed in God, now trust and believe in me also. My Father’s house has many dwelling places. If it were otherwise, I would tell you plainly, because I go to prepare a place for you to rest” (John 14:1-2 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “Do not let your hearts be troubled (distressed, agitated). You believe in and adhere to and trust in and rely on God; believe in and adhere to and trust in and rely also on Me. In My Father’s house there are many dwelling places (homes). If it were not so, I would have told you; for I am going away to prepare a place for you” (John 14:1-2 AMPC). Distressed. Agitated. Not letting the heart go there is a choice, one Jesus asked the disciples to make in the upper room and one He asks every disciple to make in every uncertain hour since.

The Greek word Jesus uses for “troubled” is tarassō. It means to be shaken up, stirred, thrown into disorder. It is the same word John uses to describe the water at the Pool of Bethesda being troubled by the angel. Jesus is naming exactly what was happening in the disciples’ hearts. They were shaken. They were stirred. Their inner world was being thrown into disorder by the news that their Master was leaving. And Jesus said, do not let that be the final state of your heart. Anchor your heart in something more stable than what you can see. Believe in God. Believe in Me. Trust the Father’s house on the other side of the trouble.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, whatever is stirring your heart in this hour, Jesus is speaking the same steadying words. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, if there is uncertainty about your health, your work, your family, your future, you are not being asked to pretend the uncertainty is not real. You are being asked to lift your gaze beyond it. Jesus is preparing your place. Whatever loss you may face, the destination on the other side is the Father’s house. Anchor your heart there. Let not your heart be troubled. Believe in God. Believe also in Him.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that Jesus has spoken over my heart the words He spoke over the disciples in the upper room. Let not your heart be troubled. I refuse to let the uncertainties of this hour become the final state of my heart. I anchor my heart in You. I trust in Jesus. I trust the Father’s house He is preparing for me. Whatever loss I may face, the destination on the other side is home. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

My heart is not troubled today. I believe in God. I believe in Jesus. He is preparing my place in the Father’s house. I anchor my heart in what He has said.
